newsitem.title: DENMARK: German data, domestic forecast hit Danish bonds.
newsitem.headline: German data, domestic forecast hit Danish bonds.

text.p: Higher than expected German money supply data and a domestic forecast of high growth and low inflation combined to depress Danish bond prices on Wednesday.
"We started a bit weak anyway without any visible reason and then the German M3 and a mildly negative Danish Wise Men's report came and poisoned the chalice altogether," a dealer said.
At 1145 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 languished at 107.99, down from Tuesday's 108.50, in turnover of 950 million crowns which suffered from a trading system fault.
Its December future fell 0.55 to 107.76, with six contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.40 point to 85.30 and the crown returned to Tuesday's level of 3.8400 to the mark, after earlier firming a little to 3.8397.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany gaped to 97 basis points compared to 93 bp 24 hours ago. --Claus Mathisen, Copenhagen newsroom,+45-33-969651
